title: Pumpkin Spice Muffins with a Crumb Top
changes_from_base: Canned pumpkin purée and a homemade cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and clove blend replace the berries and buttermilk; a buttery crumb goes on top.
summary: Moist pumpkin muffins with a homemade spice blend and a crunchy cinnamon crumb top.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Crumb
steps.text: Mix the 70 g flour, 60 g sugar, cinnamon and melted butter with a fork until it clumps. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and line the tin.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk the 320 g flour with the 250 g sugar, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: In another bowl whisk the pumpkin purée, melted butter, eggs, milk and vanilla until smooth and orange.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Fold the pumpkin mix into the flour with a spatula until no dry streaks remain.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Fill the cases, crumble the topping over and bake 22-26 min, until a skewer comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool 10 min in the tin, then on the rack.

tips: The most common mistake is using pumpkin pie filling, which is already sweetened and spiced; use plain purée.
Measure purée by weight for a consistent batter.
Mashed roasted squash can replace canned pumpkin; drain it well first.
storage: Keep in an airtight box for up to 3 days; they stay moist. Freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
